# autter_synthetic_check (Resource)

A synthetic check: Autter requests a URL on a schedule and opens a Runtime issue when it fails. Addressed by its name within the repository. Synthetic checks must be turned on for the organization (Runtime → Checks).

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "autter_repository" "web" {
  full_name = "acme/web"
}

# Header values are stored encrypted and never returned: keep them in sensitive variables.
variable "status_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "autter_synthetic_check" "health" {
  repository_id        = data.autter_repository.web.id
  name                 = "Health"
  url                  = "https://status.example.com/health"
  method               = "GET"
  expected_status      = 200
  body_contains        = "ok"
  interval_seconds     = 300
  latency_threshold_ms = 1500
  failures_to_fire     = 3
  service              = "status-page"

  headers = {
    "X-Api-Key" = var.status_api_key
  }
}

# A journey check replays a saved journey of the repository (the Journeys tab) in a
# browser against the site's address. It takes no HTTP-only attributes (method,
# headers, expected_status, body_contains, timeout_ms, latency_threshold_ms).
resource "autter_synthetic_check" "signup" {
  repository_id    = data.autter_repository.web.id
  name             = "Sign-up journey"
  kind             = "journey"
  url              = "https://app.example.com"
  journey_id       = "wj_signup"
  interval_seconds = 3600 # 900, 3600, 21600 or 86400
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The synthetic check's name, unique in the repository: the API addresses it by name. Changing it replaces the resource (a rename is a delete and a create). If a synthetic check with this name already exists, it is adopted.
- `repository_id` (String) The repository: its id, usually `data.autter_repository.<label>.id`. Its full name (`owner/repo`) also works, but after an import the id is stored, so use the id to keep plans clean. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `url` (String) An http or https address reachable from the internet. For a journey check, the site's address only (`https://app.example.com`, no path, query or fragment); the journey opens its own pages on it. Autter stores it normalized (`https://example.com` as `https://example.com/`); that is not a change.

### Optional

- `body_contains` (String) HTTP checks: text the response body must contain (GET only).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the check runs. Default `true`.
- `environment` (String) The environment the issue is filed under. Default `production`.
- `expected_status` (Number) HTTP checks: the status the check expects. Default 200. Null for a journey check.
- `failures_to_fire` (Number) Failures in a row before the check opens a Runtime issue, 1 to 10. Default 2.
- `headers` (Map of String, Sensitive) HTTP checks: request headers, at most 20. Autter stores them encrypted and never returns their values, so a value changed outside Terraform is not detected; a header added or removed outside Terraform is. Set them from sensitive variables.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) How often the check runs, in seconds. HTTP checks: 60, 300, 900 or 3600, default 300 (the free plan: 300 at the fastest). Journey checks: 900, 3600, 21600 or 86400, default 3600 (the free plan: 3600 at the fastest).
- `journey_id` (String) Journey checks: the id of the saved journey to replay. Required when `kind` is `journey`; not allowed otherwise. Only signed-out journeys that write nothing can be checked.
- `kind` (String) `http` (the default) requests `url`; `journey` replays a saved journey of the repository (the Journeys tab) in a browser against `url`. A check's kind is fixed: changing it replaces the check.
- `latency_threshold_ms` (Number) HTTP checks: a response slower than this many milliseconds counts as a failure.
- `method` (String) HTTP checks: `GET` (the default) or `HEAD`. Null for a journey check.
- `service` (String) The service the issue is filed under. Left out: the URL's host.
- `timeout_ms` (Number) HTTP checks: request timeout in milliseconds, 1000 to 30000. Default 10000. Null for a journey check.

### Read-Only

- `consecutive_failures` (Number) Failures in a row so far.
- `created_at` (String) When the synthetic check was created (ISO 8601).
- `created_by` (String) The id of the member who created the synthetic check; null for one Autter created.
- `firing` (Boolean) The check has failed `failures_to_fire` times in a row and its issue is open. Changes with every run.
- `first_passed_at` (String) Journey checks: when the check first passed against its url (ISO 8601); it opens no Runtime issue before that. Null for HTTP checks.
- `header_names` (List of String) The names of the stored headers.
- `id` (String) The synthetic check's id in Autter. Informational: the provider addresses it by repository and name.
- `issue_id` (String) The Runtime issue the check opens while it fails.
- `last_checked_at` (String) When the check last ran (ISO 8601).
- `last_duration_ms` (Number) How long the last run took, in milliseconds.
- `last_error` (String) Why the last run failed.
- `last_ok` (Boolean) Whether the last run passed. Changes with every run.
- `last_status` (Number) The HTTP status of the last run.
- `next_due_at` (String) When the check runs next (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (String) When the synthetic check was last changed (ISO 8601). It does not move when an apply changes nothing.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = autter_synthetic_check.health
  id = "acme/web:Health"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is "<repository>:<name>". Header values cannot be read back, so
# the first plan after an import updates the check once to send them.
terraform import autter_synthetic_check.health "acme/web:Health"
```
